To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the landscape response to the late Pleistocene climatic change in the NW Andes was dominated by a change in sediment supply, 2) the sediment fluxes were controlled by basin geometry and the spatial pattern of connectivity between source and sinks, and 3) the sediment flux response to the late-Pleistocene climate change was spatially heterogeneous, with the largest sediment fluxes in the headwater catchments.
(1) the sediment flux from the Andes in NW Argentina is modulated by climate change and (2) the sediment flux is controlled by basin geometry and drainage network connectivity.
(a) sediment flux from mountain ranges is highly variable in space and time, and (b) this variability is strongly controlled by the geometry and connectivity of the sedimentary basin.
